doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Childhood listening: brother Torrie's jazz records and R&B
summary: He ignored pop radio, listened to his brother's jazz records and loved R&B feel.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So Ronnie, I was looking this morning at the top ten from different years, and if my calculations are right when you were ten years old the top singers in the music were Perry Como, Frankie Laine, Dinah Shore. Okay. Six years later “Cherry Pink and Apple Blossom White,” “Rock Around the Clock,” “The Yellow Rose of Texas.” So my question is, what on the radio, if anything, grabbed you at that time, when you were like impressionable?

Oh man. Well I’ll tell you the truth, I wasn’t into a lot of pop music at all. My brother, my older brother Torrie, Torrie Zito, he was into jazz. He was a piano player. And I used to listen to his records. He would buy records and I would just zero in. But there were some pop records that I really liked. You know like — oh I mean well actually it was rhythm and blues bands. That’s what it was you know. It was really rhythm and blues.

You know like Wilson Pickett and those people in the beginning, I just loved the rhythm feel you know in those records. But yeah “Rock Around the Clock” and those, they were okay but it was more like it just struck me as being like country you know, more country than anything else. But I know the people just loved it. But that’s about it. I listened to a lot of jazz records when I was like 14 and 15, I was listening to Miles and you know, all that, Bud Powell.
